title: Why Treatments Seem to Work When They May Not

hook.en: A patient comes in with terrible pain. You treat them. Two weeks later they are better and thank you. Did your treatment work? Maybe. But four other things could also explain the recovery, and a good therapist learns to think of all five.
hook.ur: Mareez shadeed dard ke saath aata hai. Aap ilaaj karte hain. Do haftay baad woh behtar hai aur shukriya kehta hai. Kya aap ke ilaaj ne kaam kiya? Shayad. Lekin recovery ki char aur wajuhaat bhi ho sakti hain, aur achha therapist paanchon ke baare mein sochna seekhta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll name five reasons a treatment can look effective without being so (natural history, regression to the mean, placebo and context, co-interventions, confounding), explain why control groups exist, and talk about this honestly with patients.
goal.ur: End tak aap paanch wajuhaat batayenge jin ki wajah se ilaaj kaam karta lagta hai bina asar ke (natural history, regression to the mean, placebo aur context, co-interventions, confounding), samjhayenge ke control groups kyun hote hain, aur mareezon se is par imaandari se baat karenge.

text.en: Most painful problems **improve by themselves** over time. People also tend to seek help when they feel **worst**, and then drift back towards their usual level. Add the effect of care, attention and belief, and almost every treatment looks successful in a before-and-after story. A control group is the only way to separate **what the treatment did** from **what would have happened anyway**.
text.ur: Zyada tar dardnak masail **khud behtar** hote hain waqt ke saath. Log aksar tab madad lene aate hain jab woh **sab se bura** mehsoos karte hain, aur phir apni aam satah ki taraf wapas aa jate hain. Is mein care, tawajjo aur yaqeen ka asar jodein to taqreeban har ilaaj before-and-after kahani mein kamyab lagta hai. Control group wahid tareeqa hai jis se alag kiya ja sake ke **ilaaj ne kya kiya** aur **waise bhi kya hota**.

text.en: Think of a **rain-dance and the monsoon**. The dancers dance, and then it rains, so the dance "worked". But the monsoon would have come anyway. Unless you compare with a village that did not dance, you cannot know. A before-and-after patient story is a rain-dance story.
text.ur: **Barish ka naach aur mansoon** sochein. Naachne wale naachte hain, phir barish hoti hai, to naach "kaam kar gaya". Lekin mansoon to aana hi tha. Jab tak aap us gaon se muqabla na karein jis ne nahi nacha, aap nahi jaan sakte. Before-and-after mareez ki kahani barish ke naach ki kahani hai.

title.en: Five reasons a treatment looks like it worked
title.ur: Paanch wajuhaat ke ilaaj kaam karta lagta hai

rows.en: The problem would have improved by itself
rows.ur: Masla khud hi behtar ho jata

rows.en: Most sprains and acute back pain settle within weeks regardless of treatment
rows.ur: Zyada tar moch aur acute peeth dard haftoon mein ilaaj ke baghair theek ho jate hain

rows.en: Extreme scores drift back towards average on their own
rows.ur: Intehai scores khud average ki taraf wapas aate hain

rows.en: Patients come when pain is at its worst, so it will likely fall whatever we do
rows.ur: Mareez tab aate hain jab dard sab se zyada hota hai, isliye hum kuch bhi karein woh girega

rows.en: Belief, attention and ritual change symptoms, especially pain
rows.ur: Yaqeen, tawajjo aur rasam alamaat badalti hain, khaaskar dard

rows.en: A caring clinician, a warm room and a machine with lights can reduce pain
rows.ur: Mohabbat bhara clinician, garam kamra aur batiyon wali machine dard kam kar sakte hain

rows.en: Other things changed at the same time
rows.ur: Saath hi doosri cheezein badal gayin

rows.en: The patient also took a painkiller, rested and changed their desk
rows.ur: Mareez ne dard ki goli li, aaram kiya aur apna desk badla

rows.en: A third factor explains both the treatment and the result
rows.ur: Teesri wajah ilaaj aur nateeje dono ko samjhati hai

rows.en: Motivated patients attend more sessions and also recover better for other reasons
rows.ur: Jazbe wale mareez zyada sessions mein aate hain aur doosri wajuhaat se bhi behtar hote hain

question.en: A patient comes to clinic on the day his back pain is worst and is much better two weeks later after your treatment. Which explanation is most likely at work besides your treatment?
question.ur: Mareez peeth dard ke sab se bure din clinic aata hai aur do haftay baad aap ke ilaaj ke baad bohat behtar hai. Aap ke ilaaj ke ilawa kaun si wazahat sab se zyada imkaan rakhti hai?

text.en: Natural history and regression to the mean
text.ur: Natural history aur regression to the mean

feedback.en: Yes — pain is likely to fall from its peak even without treatment.
feedback.ur: Haan — dard apni intehai satah se ilaaj ke baghair bhi girne ka imkaan rakhta hai.

text.en: Only a placebo effect, so the treatment did nothing
text.ur: Sirf placebo, yani ilaaj ne kuch nahi kiya

feedback.en: You cannot conclude that either without a control group.
feedback.ur: Control group ke baghair yeh bhi nahi keh sakte.

text.en: Only that your treatment was brilliant
text.ur: Sirf yeh ke aap ka ilaaj shandar tha

feedback.en: Other explanations must be ruled out first.
feedback.ur: Pehle doosri wajuhaat khaarij karni chahiye.

question.en: A trial compares a new exercise programme with no treatment. The exercise group improves more. A critic says part of the gain may be due to attention and enthusiasm. What does the critic want?
question.ur: Ek trial nayi exercise programme ka muqabla koi ilaaj na dene se karta hai. Exercise group zyada behtar hota hai. Ek naqqad kehta hai ke faida ka kuch hissa tawajjo aur josh ki wajah se ho sakta hai. Naqqad kya chahta hai?

text.en: A larger group of enthusiastic patients

feedback.en: More enthusiasm does not remove the problem.
feedback.ur: Zyada josh masla door nahi karta.

text.en: A longer follow-up with no comparison group
text.ur: Bina comparison group ke lamba follow-up

feedback.en: Without a comparison, the problem remains.
feedback.ur: Comparison ke baghair masla rehta hai.

text.en: A comparison group that gets equal attention but a different or inactive treatment
text.ur: Aisa comparison group jisay barabar tawajjo mile lekin mukhtalif ya ghair-faal ilaaj

feedback.en: Yes — this separates the treatment's specific effect from the attention effect.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh ilaaj ke khaas asar ko tawajjo ke asar se alag karta hai.

question.en: Which statement about the placebo effect is most accurate?
question.ur: Placebo asar ke baare mein kaun sa bayan sab se durust hai?

text.en: It only works with dummy pills
text.ur: Yeh sirf nakli goliyon se kaam karta hai

feedback.en: Rituals, devices and words can all have context effects.
feedback.ur: Rasam, aale aur alfaaz sab ka context asar ho sakta hai.

text.en: Context and expectation can genuinely change symptoms such as pain, but we cannot assume they change the underlying disease
text.ur: Context aur umeed dard jaisi alamaat ko haqeeqatan badal sakti hain, lekin yeh farz nahi kar sakte ke bunyadi bimari badalti hai

feedback.en: Yes — it is real for symptoms, but it is not a cure for the disease itself.
feedback.ur: Haan — alamaat ke liye haqeeqi hai, lekin bimari ka ilaaj nahi.

text.en: It is imaginary, so patients who respond are faking
text.ur: Yeh khayali hai, isliye jawab dene wale mareez dikhawa kar rahe hain

feedback.ur: Jawab dene wale dikhawa nahi karte.

text.en: **Treating a good outcome as proof of a good treatment.** "My patient got better after ultrasound, so ultrasound works" confuses sequence with cause. A related trap is to treat the placebo effect as an insult. Context effects are real and can be used ethically, with warmth, clear explanation and realistic expectations, alongside treatments that have evidence.
text.ur: **Achhe nateeje ko achhe ilaaj ka saboot samajhna.** "Mere mareez ne ultrasound ke baad behtari ki, isliye ultrasound kaam karta hai" tarteeb ko wajah samajhta hai. Isse jura jaal placebo ko tauheen samajhna hai. Context asar haqeeqi hain aur akhlaqi taur par istemal ho sakte hain, garam jazbe, saaf wazahat aur haqeeqat pasand umeedon ke saath, un ilajon ke saath jin ke paas evidence hai.

text.en: **Be honest and kind.** For example: "Most back pain gets better by itself over a few weeks. I want to use things that help you move and feel confident, and I will tell you if something is likely to be just a comfort." This builds trust without promising miracles, and protects you from taking credit or blame for what nature did.
text.ur: **Imaandar aur naram rahein.** Misaal: "Zyada tar peeth dard chand haftoon mein khud behtar ho jata hai. Main woh cheezein istemal karna chahta hoon jo aap ko harkat karne aur itminan se rehne mein madad karein, aur agar kuch sirf rahat ke liye ho to main bata dunga." Isse mojize ka waada kiye baghair bharosa banta hai, aur aap qudrat ke kiye ka kredit ya ilzam lene se bachte hain.

question.en: If most problems get better by themselves, why do we treat them at all?
question.ur: Agar zyada tar masail khud behtar ho jate hain to hum ilaaj kyun karte hain?

answer.en: Good care can speed recovery, reduce suffering, restore confidence, prevent a relapse, and find the few who will not recover on their own. The skill is knowing which problems need active treatment, and being honest about which benefits are small.
answer.ur: Achhi care recovery tez kar sakti hai, takleef kam kar sakti hai, itminan bahal kar sakti hai, dobara hone se rok sakti hai, aur un chand logon ko dhoondh sakti hai jo khud theek nahi honge. Hunar yeh jaanna hai ke kin masail ko faal ilaaj chahiye, aur kin faide chhote hain unke baare mein imaandar rehna.

beats.patient: A physiotherapist introduces a new device for tennis elbow. Over three months, 8 of 10 patients get better, and she tells colleagues it works. A colleague asks, "Compared with what?"
beats.assessment: Without a comparison group, she cannot separate the device from natural recovery, regression to the mean, placebo and other changes.
beats.treatment: She could compare her results with patients treated by usual care or a different method, keep a record of outcomes, and look for published controlled trials of the device.
beats.reassess: She finds that controlled trials show little difference from sham, and she keeps the device optional while focusing on exercise and education.

text.en: **Never let a "good outcome" story delay a referral.** A patient who improves for a few days may still have a serious cause. If pain is unexplained, worsening, nocturnal, or comes with weight loss, fever or neurological signs, refer, whatever the early response to treatment. A placebo response does not rule out serious disease.
text.ur: **"Achhe nateeje" ki kahani ko refer mein der na karne dein.** Jo mareez chand din behtar rahe woh phir bhi seriyas wajah rakh sakta hai. Agar dard be-wajah, barhta hua, raat ka ho, ya wazan kam hona, bukhar ya neurological nishaniyon ke saath ho to refer karein, ilaaj ka shuruaati jawab kuch bhi ho. Placebo jawab seriyas bimari ko khaarij nahi karta.

text.en: A Cochrane review of placebo interventions found little evidence that placebos have powerful clinical effects in general, but possible small effects on subjective outcomes such as pain, which are also more affected by bias. The Lancet review by Finniss and colleagues described that the context around a treatment, including words, rituals and the therapeutic relationship, can produce real neurobiological changes. Regression to the mean is the statistical tendency for extreme measurements to move closer to average on re-measurement, and it affects any study that selects patients because their scores are extreme.
text.ur: Placebo interventions ke ek Cochrane review ko is baat ke kam saboot mile ke placebo aam taur par taqatwar clinical asar rakhte hain, lekin dard jaise subjective nateejon par mumkin chhote asar, jo bias se bhi zyada mutasir hote hain. Finniss aur saathiyon ke Lancet review ne batayi ke ilaaj ke gird ka context, jis mein alfaaz, rasam aur therapeutic rishta shamil hain, haqeeqi neurobiological tabdeeliyan paida kar sakta hai. Regression to the mean woh shumariyati rujhan hai jis mein intehai paimaishein dobara naapne par average ke qareeb jati hain, aur yeh har us study ko mutasir karta hai jo mareez is liye chunti hai ke unke scores intehai hain.

text.en: **N-R-P-C-C.** Natural history, Regression to the mean, Placebo and context, Co-interventions, Confounding: five reasons a treatment can look good.
text.ur: **N-R-P-C-C.** Natural history, Regression to the mean, Placebo aur context, Co-interventions, Confounding: paanch wajuhaat ke ilaaj achha lagta hai.

summary.en: Natural history, regression to the mean, context, co-interventions and confounding can all make a treatment look effective.
summary.ur: Natural history, regression to the mean, context, co-interventions aur confounding sab ilaaj ko mu'assir dikha sakte hain.

summary.en: Only a fair comparison group separates what the treatment did from what would have happened anyway.
summary.ur: Sirf munsifana comparison group alag karta hai ke ilaaj ne kya kiya aur waise bhi kya hota.

summary.en: Context effects are real, can be used ethically, and never replace safe assessment or referral.
summary.ur: Context asar haqeeqi hain, akhlaqi taur par istemal ho sakte hain, aur mehfooz assessment ya refer ki jagah kabhi nahi lete.

front.en: What is regression to the mean?
front.ur: Regression to the mean kya hai?

back.en: Extreme scores tend to move back towards average on their own.
back.ur: Intehai scores khud average ki taraf wapas aate hain.

front.en: Name the five reasons a treatment may look effective without working.
front.ur: Paanch wajuhaat batayein ke ilaaj bina asar ke mu'assir kyun lagta hai.

back.en: Natural history, regression to the mean, placebo and context, co-interventions, confounding.
back.ur: Natural history, regression to the mean, placebo aur context, co-interventions, confounding.

front.en: Why do we need control groups?

back.en: To separate the treatment's effect from what would have happened anyway.
back.ur: Ilaaj ke asar ko us se alag karne ke liye jo waise bhi hota.

back.en: No; context effects are real, especially for pain, but do not cure disease.
back.ur: Nahi; context asar haqeeqi hain, khaaskar dard mein, lekin bimari theek nahi karte.

note.ur: Controlled trials kaise madad karte hain.

note.en: Talking honestly about what hands-on care does.
note.ur: Hands-on care kya karti hai us par imaandari se baat.
